Norman Read, and exile Englishman from Steyning, walking in the colours of New Zealand, took the bronze medal in 2 hours 46 minutes 48.2 seconds.

All the great British long distance walkers and many of those from abroad have competed in this race, including Olympic medallists Tommy Green, Harold Whitlock, Lloyd Johnson, Don Thompson, Norman Read and Abdon Pamich.

Steyning is a village nestling under the Northern slopes of the South Downs which has a walking tradition extending over many decades and has indeed produced one Olympic Champion, Norman Read, who won the 50 kilos walk in 1960 wearing the colours of New Zealand.

A very emotional evening finished up by the taxi driver announcing that a countryman of his had won a gold medal in 1956 - who else but the late Norman Read who had been so much in our minds during our stay.
